newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 19.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech National Bank is currently having discussions about the value of the crown and the best way for the bank to react to it. The director of the central bank's exchange policy, Jiri Pospisil, stated that the bank would like to see the crown closer to parity. He did not rule out decreasing the bank's basic rates or direct intervention on the market in order to decrease interest of foreign investors in the crown.
- The average cost of water increased last year by 13.6 percent. Households paid about 16 percent more for their water than in 1995, and other customers paid over 11 percent more.

- The director of the department for financial policy at the Finance Ministry, Pavel Stepanek, stated yesterday that this year's inflation rate could reach nine percent due to expected price deregulations.

PRAVO - The Agrarian Chamber, of which most farmers in the Czech Republic are members, has decided to react to the fact that the cabinet is not resolving farmer's requests. In a meeting on Monday, the chamber recommended farmers in all regions to accuse the cabinet of civic disobedience.

- The British brewery Bass denied the fact that it has nearly reached an agreement with Investicni a Postovni Banka for another 34 percent of shares in Radegast Nosovice brewery. IPB is currently the largest shareholder of Radegast, while Bass owns 33 percent of the brewery.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Yesterday, nearly one fourth of teachers in chosen areas participated in the chain strike, which is so far the smallest number. The school workers union will meet on Friday to discuss the strike, but Education Minister Ivan Pilip still refuses to grant the union its main request, which is to appeal to the cabinet for more money for wages.

- The new system for financing health services could force hospitals to send patients home as soon as possible and hope that they will return soon. According to the system, which the Health Ministry is preparing, hospitals would recieve determined amounts from insurance companies according to what ailment the patient has, how payment is made, and how many patients are examined.

- After many disagreements, Prvni Brnenska Strojirna completed the sale to Asea Brown Boveri of its share in the collective company ABB-PBS. The nominal price of the stake in the collective company, which was established four years ago, exceeded 366 million crowns.
